newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Assembly meets after court rules against Plavsic.
newsitem.headline: Assembly meets after court rules against Plavsic.

text.p: The Bosnian Serb parliament, dominated by nationalists loyal to indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic, began a crisis session on Friday in defiance of an order by President Biljana Plavsic disbanding it.

The Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA said before the session began that constitutional court had ruled the government could ignore Plavsic's decision and her call for general elections in an attempt to break the power of Karadzic and his hardline allies.

The government has threatened to use parliament to remove Plavsic from power over her allegations that Karadzic and senior aides are involved in widespread corruption and obstruction of the peace process in Bosnia.
She remain at her office in the northern town of Banja Luka while the parliament convened in an hotel near the hardline stronghold of Pale outside Sarajevo.
Western mediators have backed Plavsic in the struggle, fearing that victory for the nationalists could further damage the slow-moving peace process in Bosnia.

The parliament session was apparently not attended by Serb opposition deputies or the 14 legislators of the Moslem SDA party, who left the field clear for the ruling SDS which is covertly controlled by Karadzic.
